statement: A data set of $10$ numbers has a mean of $24$. When one more number is added to the data set, the mean of the $11$ numbers is $26$. What number was added?

choices.misconception: I subtracted the two means, $26 - 24$, as if the added number were the change in the mean.
I multiplied both means by 10, so I found $260 - 240 = 20$, but there are 11 numbers after the new one is added.
I multiplied both means by 11, so I found $286 - 264 = 22$, but the original sum comes from only 10 numbers.

hints: A mean times the number of values gives the sum of the values.
Find the sum of the $10$ original numbers and the sum of all $11$ numbers. The added number is the difference.
The original sum is $10 \cdot 24 = 240$ and the new sum is $11 \cdot 26 = 286$.

solutions.reliable: The $10$ original numbers add to $10 \cdot 24 = 240$. All $11$ numbers add to $11 \cdot 26 = 286$. The added number is $286 - 240 = 46$. Check: $\dfrac{240 + 46}{11} = \dfrac{286}{11} = 26$.
solutions.elegant: The $10$ original numbers are, on average, $2$ below the new mean of $26$, a total of $20$ below. The added number must make up for that, so it is $26 + 20 = 46$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
